Home.headline: Understand technology. Lead the decision.
Home.subhead: A selective 16-week immersion for founders, directors and managers who have to evaluate AI, challenge a vendor and drive a digital transformation, without becoming engineers.
Home.positioningTitle: You do not need to become an engineer.
Home.positioningBody: You need to understand technology well enough to ask the right question, weigh an option, recognise a risk and defend a decision.
Home.positioningClosing: Digital literacy is becoming leadership literacy.
Home.audienceTitle: Built for people who carry responsibility
Home.audienceSubtitle: Three profiles, one shared need: deciding well once technology enters the equation.
Home.capabilitiesSubtitle: Not a catalogue of tools. A system of judgment that outlives the hype cycle.
Home.methodSubtitle: The facilitator does not hand you the answer. They help you learn how to find it, test it and defend it.
Home.journeyTitle: Four phases, sixteen weeks, one transformation challenge
Home.journeySubtitle: Every week starts from a real problem and ends with a deliverable you can take back to your organisation.
Home.admissionsSubtitle: We are not trying to fill seats. We are looking for people ready to learn, contribute and be challenged.
Home.finalTitle: The world does not need more leaders who know the vocabulary of technology.
Home.finalSubtitle: It needs leaders who know what to do with it.

Admissions.title: Not everyone needs this programme
Admissions.subtitle: We care more about the quality of the cohort than about the number of participants.
Admissions.fitTitle: This programme is for you if
fit: You hold real responsibility and have a concrete problem to investigate.
You stay curious about what you do not yet understand.
You accept being challenged, and challenge your peers with respect.
You can commit across the full 16 weeks.
Admissions.notFitTitle: It is probably not for you if
notFit: You want a video library to consume passively.
You are looking for programming training.
You cannot attend the live sessions.

Cohort.subtitle: The first cohort stays deliberately small. That is a teaching decision, not artificial scarcity.

Pricing.paymentAfter: Payment is only requested once your application has been accepted.

Payment.title: How payment works
Payment.subtitle: Applying costs nothing. Payment only comes up once you have been admitted.

apply.title: Application
apply.body: Free and non-binding. You describe your context and the challenge you want to work on.

conversation.title: Conversation
conversation.body: You book a twenty to thirty minute slot to check the programme fits your situation. The Google Meet link reaches you as soon as the appointment is confirmed.

admission.title: Admission decision
admission.body: You get a clear answer. If it is positive, your admission letter states the amount, the schedule and how to settle it.

payment.title: Settlement
payment.body: In full or in two instalments. Your seat is confirmed once the first payment arrives.

Payment.methodsBody: Accepted payment methods and settlement details are sent with your admission letter. No payment information is requested before admission.
Payment.refundBody: Because the cohort is capped, a confirmed seat is removed from availability. Withdrawal terms are set out in the admission letter, before any payment.
Payment.orderBody: The conversation has to happen before settlement is completed. We never confirm a seat on the strength of a payment alone: the exchange exists precisely to check, on both sides, that the programme is the right one.
Payment.bookNote: Twenty to thirty minute slots, by video call.

Prerequisites.title: What you need to take part
Prerequisites.subtitle: Nothing exotic. But these are not optional: the method depends on you actually participating.

device.title: A computer
device.body: Live sessions, deliverables and peer review all happen on a computer. A phone is not enough to produce the deliverables.

connection.title: A stable connection
connection.body: Enough for one weekly video call with camera on. Written resources stay available offline.

time.title: 3 to 5 hours a week
time.body: Live session included. Project weeks ask for 5 to 7. This is the most common reason people drop out, so assess it honestly.

problem.title: A real problem
problem.body: You arrive with a concrete challenge from your organisation. It runs through all sixteen weeks and becomes the basis of your final defence.

language.title: The working language
language.body: Live sessions are facilitated in French, and international technical vocabulary (API, cloud, SaaS) is explained as it comes up. More comfortable in English? You are welcome: the written resources exist in both languages, and you can ask your questions, write your deliverables and give your final defence in English. Mention it during the admission conversation and we will prepare the cohort accordingly.

posture.title: Openness to challenge
posture.body: Your reasoning will be contested by your peers and by the facilitator. That is the core of the method, not an accident.

Corporate.title: Having a seat funded by your organisation
Corporate.body: An organisation can enrol one employee, or several. The application stays individual and the selection unchanged: it is the person who joins the cohort, not the company. Mention it in your application or write to us, and we will arrange the conversation with the people involved.
